Theorem
[Toponogov comparison theorem, 1959]

Source: petersen:page-0463, petersen:page-0464, petersen:page-0467, petersen:page-0468, petersen:page-0469, petersen:page-0470 ↗ def:pet-ch12-hinge ↗ def:pet-ch12-triangle ↗ lem:pet-ch12-comparison-hinge-triangle-exist 1. ch12:12.2.2Let $(M,g)$ be a complete Riemannian manifold with $\sec \ge k$.

  • Hinge version. For any hinge with vertices $p,x,y\in M$ forming angle $\alpha $ at $x$, and any comparison hinge in $S_k^n$ with vertices $p_k,x_k,y_k$ (section 2), $|py|\le |p_ky_k|$.

  • Triangle version. For any triangle in $M$, the interior angles are no smaller than the corresponding interior angles of a comparison triangle in $S_k^n$.

Proof

↗ thm:pet-ch12-toponogov ↗ prop:pet-ch12-law-of-cosines ↗ lem:pet-ch12-hessian-comparison \sketch The triangle statement follows from the hinge statement and the model law of cosines in section 2: with two sides fixed, increasing the opposite side increases the included angle.

For the hinge, fix a geodesic in $M$ and a model geodesic with prescribed initial distance and radial derivative. By section 2, for $k=0$ the distance-function difference has nonnegative second derivative, while for $k=-1$ it satisfies $\psi ''\ge \psi $. For $k=1$, compare with $\zeta ''=-(1+\varepsilon )\zeta $ and use a support-function maximum argument until $\zeta $ vanishes. Letting $\varepsilon $ and the initial perturbation tend to zero proves the hinge inequality.

□
